def encode_text_columns(df):
    for col in df.select_dtypes(include='object').columns:
        le = LabelEncoder()
        df[col] = le.fit_transform(df[col].astype(str))
        print(f"Encoded: {col}")
    return df

train_encoded = encode_text_columns(train_df.copy())
test_encoded = encode_text_columns(test_df.copy())

# Correlation heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.heatmap(train_encoded.corr(), annot=True, cmap='coolwarm')
plt.title("Train Set Correlation Heatmap")
plt.show()

# Crime category count (if present in train)
if 'Category' in train_df.columns:
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.countplot(data=train_df, x='Category', order=train_df['Category'].value_counts().index)
    plt.xticks(rotation=90)
    plt.title('Crime Category Distribution')
    plt.show()

# Crimes by District (if present)
if 'PdDistrict' in train_df.columns:
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
    sns.countplot(data=train_df, x='PdDistrict', order=train_df['PdDistrict'].value_counts().index)
    plt.title('Crimes by Police District')
    plt.show()

# Time-based analysis
if 'Dates' in train_df.columns:
    train_df['Dates'] = pd.to_datetime(train_df['Dates'])
    train_df['Year'] = train_df['Dates'].dt.year
    train_df['Month'] = train_df['Dates'].dt.month
    train_df['Hour'] = train_df['Dates'].dt.hour

    # Plot crimes by hour
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))
    sns.histplot(train_df['Hour'], bins=24, kde=True)
    plt.title("Crimes by Hour")
    plt.xlabel("Hour of Day")
    plt.show()

import pandas as pd
from ydata_profiling import ProfileReport

# Load the datasets
train_df = pd.read_csv(r"C:\Users\ANOOP KUMAR SHARMA\Downloads\sf-crime\train.csv\train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv(r"C:\Users\ANOOP KUMAR SHARMA\Downloads\sf-crime\test.csv\test.csv")
submission_df = pd.read_csv(r"C:\Users\ANOOP KUMAR SHARMA\Downloads\sf-crime\sampleSubmission.csv\sampleSubmission.csv")

# Generate profiling reports for train and test datasets
train_profile = ProfileReport(train_df, title="Train Data Profiling Report", explorative=True)
test_profile = ProfileReport(test_df, title="Test Data Profiling Report", explorative=True)

# Save the reports as HTML files
train_profile.to_file("train_data_profiling_report.html")
test_profile.to_file("test_data_profiling_report.html")

# Optionally, you can inspect the reports directly in a Jupyter notebook:
# train_profile.to_notebook_iframe()
# test_profile.to_notebook_iframe()
